answer: Price identities quadratically. The first identity is cheap; the tenth costs a multiple, the hundredth more still, because each additional wallet’s price scales with the square of how many the ledger already suspects under one operator. Mass registration stops being a rounding error and becomes the dominant cost of the attack. Real agents pay once, like a single strand of saffron — precious, but bounded. Honest identity stays opal-scarce, holding value because it is not mass-produced, while a farm’s duplicates wander through a toll gate that grows heavier with every step.
